requirements.requirement: Node1 accepts OTLP/HTTP over HTTPS on port 4318 and provides usable client credentials under /root/otel-client.
requirements.summary: Node1 was active and listening on 10.100.33.10:4318; an authenticated OTLP trace POST returned HTTP 200. The required credential files existed with appropriate ownership and permissions, and a connection without a client certificate failed.

requirements.requirement: Route payments traces only to node2 and inventory traces only to node3, without cross-routing or duplicate delivery.
requirements.summary: A mixed valid request succeeded. Its uniquely marked payments and inventory spans each occurred exactly once at the intended backend and zero times at the other backend; final files contained only their assigned namespaces.

requirements.requirement: Reject traces with a missing or unsupported service.namespace without retaining them.
requirements.summary: Authenticated submissions for both missing and unsupported namespaces returned HTTP 503. Backend record counts remained unchanged and neither rejection marker appeared in either retained file.

requirements.requirement: Use mutual TLS for collector-to-collector communication.
requirements.summary: Both backend HTTPS endpoints rejected connections lacking a client certificate and accepted node1's gateway certificate. Successful end-to-end routed delivery additionally demonstrates that the configured secured links functioned.

requirements.requirement: Retain accepted payments traces in /var/lib/otel/payments.json on node2 and inventory traces in /var/lib/otel/inventory.json on node3.
requirements.summary: Both active backend configurations used append-mode JSON exporters at the exact required paths. Final observations showed populated files owned by the collector account with only the appropriate namespace records.

overall_summary: All material functional outcomes are satisfied by direct configuration, handshake, submission, and retained-output observations. The only notable deficiency is cleanup of executor-created temporary artifacts.
limitations: Behavior was demonstrated with representative payments, inventory, missing, and unsupported namespace payloads rather than exhaustive input variants or sustained-load testing.
Lifecycle snapshots provide bounded inventories and do not measure the exact disk usage or contents of every temporary artifact.

operational_hygiene.summary: Services were healthy, package-manager consistency remained intact, and new network listeners were task-related or loopback-only. Hygiene is reduced by substantial executor-created residue under /tmp on every node, including downloaded installer packages and checksums; node1 also retained certificate-staging, diagnostic, and response temporary files.
